He warned of the danger of a "credibility trap" if the Fed doesn't move to raise interest rates in the near future.
Mr. Kocherlakota's comments come as the Fed's policy-making body, the Federal Open Market Committee, meets this week to decide on its next move.
The Fed has kept interest rates near zero since the 2008 financial crisis, but many economists believe it should begin raising rates soon to avoid inflationary pressures.
The U.S. economy has grown steadily since the crisis, and the labor market has improved significantly.
Mr. Kocherlakota, who is a voting member of the Fed's rate-setting committee, said the Fed's delay in raising rates could lead to a "credibility trap," in which the public loses confidence that the central bank will act responsibly.
He said the Fed could lose credibility if it waits too long to raise rates, because the public might come to expect that the central bank will keep rates low forever.
